title: Check yourself: The life cycle, and a spec you can test

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A team's nightly report job started returning slightly different summaries after a provider released an update. The code names its model with a moving alias. What does the page say is the underlying mistake?

options.text: The job should have been interactive, so that a person could review its output live
options.says: Ruled out because the symptom has nothing to do with live review, and the maintain routine is to "re-run the evaluation set against the new model".

options.text: A deliberate pin was missing, so behaviour moved without a regression run
options.says: An alias that moves "changes behaviour under you", and the routine is to pin an id and change it on purpose, with a regression run.

options.text: The summaries were never written down as requirements before the first prompt was tried
options.says: Ruled out because a missing spec is a separate fault, while the symptom is described by "a silent change of model is a silent change of behaviour".

options.text: The nightly schedule should have been replaced by a fixed monthly cost budget for the job
options.says: Ruled out because a cost budget does not decide which model answers, and the page's fix is to "pin the model id" in configuration.

origin.section: Maintain: models retire and limits change

questions.stem: A client library crashes whenever the API adds a new field to a response, although the API's documented rules allow additions. What is the best fix?

options.text: Pin an older API version header to stop any new property from appearing in the reply body
options.says: Ruled out because earlier versions are deprecated and "may be unavailable for new users", and additions arrive within the current one.

options.text: Ask the provider to announce each new addition before it is released to the public
options.says: Ruled out because the policy already says Anthropic "may add additional values to the output", so no announcement is promised.

options.text: Wrap every call in a retry so that the crash is repeated until it clears for good
options.says: Ruled out because "a retry cannot help, because the same reply is parsed the same way again".

options.text: Take only the properties the code needs and skip everything else in the reply
options.says: The page says to be tolerant of additions and strict about what you send, which means reading only what the code uses.
